title: Benefits of having a home gym: Zero distractions
summary: He argues a home gym removes commercial-gym distractions: sharing and waiting for equipment, people talking to you mid-set, hostile gym staff and no-drop rules, attractive gym-goers, terrible pop music and announcements, and the wasted walking time in a big space. He says the thousands he spent on his home gym were worth it just to avoid gym staff.

claims.claim: Owning your training space greatly increases your ability to make gains.
In a commercial gym your schedule depends on others: you must share equipment and wait if the bench or rack is taken.
Bullying people off equipment is easy but bad behaviour that can get you banned.
People have started talking to him mid-rep while he was overhead pressing 150; the overhead press seems to attract chatty people.
He has a bad history with gym staff; in gyms with 'don't drop the weights' rules you can say goodbye to deadlifts, and staff have interrupted his heavy sets.
He spent thousands of dollars on his home gym and considers every penny worth it just to avoid gym staff.
Attractive people at the gym are a distraction that takes energy away from lifting, and chatting people up means you're no longer training.
Giving up the gym's social contact is a sacrifice you have to be ready to make to improve your physique.
Commercial gym pop music bleeds through headphones, so you crank the volume and risk your hearing; at home you can lift in silence or play your own music.
His university gym made loudspeaker announcements every 15 minutes, so nobody listened, including once when it was a real fire evacuation during his front squats.
Big gyms waste time walking between machines, fetching plates and locker rooms, which costs focus, pump, warm-up and strength; at home everything is right there.
